item.title: Beijing forum calls for open, collaborative, inclusive ecosystem for financial development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
Beijing forum calls for open, collaborative, inclusive ecosystem for financial development BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- High-profile guests gathered in Beijing on Monday for the opening of the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2026. With a theme of "Building an Open, Collaborative and Inclusive Ecosystem for Global Financial Development," this year's conference is attracting prominent guests from home and abroad who will participate in various activities, including the main forum, parallel forums, thematic conferences and side events during the four-day event. During the opening ceremony, Yin Li, secretary of the Communist Party of China Beijing Municipal Committee, said that Beijing has become an important bridge connecting Chinese and foreign financial markets. He said the capital city is ready to deepen financial exchanges and practical cooperation with all parties, jointly build an open and interconnected financial market ecosystem, and create a world-class business environment that is market-oriented, law-based, convenient and internationalized. The forum, inaugurated in 2012 as a platform for global exchange and cooperation in the field of finance, has grown into a major source of updates on China's financial policies, providing a window into the work priorities of the financial sector in the world's second-largest economy. Pan Gongsheng, governor of the People's Bank of China, China's central bank, said the central bank has actively promoted the transformation and improvement of China's monetary policy framework, further enriched its monetary policy toolkit, and made the market-based interest rate regulation mechanism clearer. Going forward, the central bank will assess and improve the monetary policy framework, continue to raise the level of RMB internationalization, further strengthen high-quality policy supply, and explore the application of artificial intelligence in areas such as assisting with monetary policy situation analysis and financial risk identification. Pan also unveiled that the central bank will join with other financial authorities to introduce a number of policy measures. These include establishing a liquidity support facility to address large-scale redemptions by non-bank institutions, expanding the range of institutions eligible for the Standing Lending Facility, and promoting connectivity between the interbank and exchange bond markets. Other policy measures to be introduced include pilot measures to facilitate foreign financial institutions' RMB purchase and sale business in the onshore foreign exchange market, and issuing guidelines regarding financial support for building international science and technology innovation centers in Beijing (Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region), Shanghai (the Yangtze River Delta), and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, according to Pan. Ding Xiangqun, head of the National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA), said that the NFRA is enhancing the effectiveness of regulation, adopting a risk-based approach to strengthen financial supervision, improving the financial rule of law in line with practical needs, and strengthening regulatory capacity in key areas. Ding said the NFRA remains committed to actively expanding new space for financial opening-up, supporting international economic and trade exchanges, and improving the global financial governance system. Regarding the capital market, Wu Qing, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), said the CSRC will make every effort to safeguard its safety and stability by closely tracking market dynamics at home and abroad, strengthening risk assessment and the policy toolkit, and enhancing risk prevention for new types of businesses. According to him, China will facilitate cross-border investment and financing by enhancing the convenience of investment operations through the Qualified Foreign Institutional Investors scheme. Foreign-funded entities are encouraged to leverage their parent companies' professional expertise and strengths to further refine their product portfolios and participate in innovative business areas in China, Wu added. Fu Hua, president of Xinhua News Agency, said at the opening ceremony that creating a favorable public opinion climate for financial reform and development is an important part of building a new ecosystem for financial development, adding that Xinhua stands ready to make an effort toward that end. Zhu Hexin, head of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), said a batch of incremental measures will be rolled out to better support enterprises in engaging in international cooperation and competition. These include facilitation measures for the current account to better meet the diverse settlement needs of foreign trade enterprises and support the development of new forms and models of trade, and measures to optimize foreign exchange management under the capital account to better meet enterprises' needs for cross-border investment, financing and fund allocation, and expand two-way investment cooperation. Zhu revealed that China intends to expand its pilot program that allows securities companies to conduct foreign exchange settlement and sales business, and support financial institutions in providing exchange rate risk management services to enterprises. The annual conference, which runs from Oct. 19 to 22, is jointly hosted by the Beijing Municipal People's Government, the People's Bank of China, the NFRA, the CSRC, Xinhua News Agency and the SAFE. item.title: Xi-proposed principles provide practical guidance for settling Africa's hotspot issues: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
Xi-proposed principles provide practical guidance for settling Africa's hotspot issues: spokesperson BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- Four principles proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping on the constructive participation of relevant parties in the resolution of African hotspot issues provide practical guidance for addressing issues including the current situation in the Horn of Africa, a foreign ministry spokesperson said on Monday. Xi put forward the principles during his meeting with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé in Beijing last week. When asked whether this was related to the current situation in northern Ethiopia, Mao Ning, the spokesperson, told a regular press briefing that the principles provide practical guidance for addressing issues including the current situation in the Horn of Africa. First, upholding Africa's leadership, Mao said, citing the principles. "African people are the true masters of the continent and should therefore play a central role in regional affairs." Second, safeguarding equity and justice. Parties should observe the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of countries concerned, she said. Third, ceasing hostilities and building peace. "War and unilateral sanctions are never real solutions to disputes between states. Countries should respect each other, engage in extensive consultation, seek common ground despite differences, and practice mutual understanding and accommodation," Mao said. "Fourth, addressing both symptoms and root causes. Addressing immediate security concerns should go hand in hand with long-term development planning," the spokesperson said. item.title: China's Q3 economy picks up pace, reinforcing role as global growth engine
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
China's Q3 economy picks up pace, reinforcing role as global growth engine An aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 18, 2026 shows a view of Tianjin Port in Tianjin, north China. (Xinhua/Sun Fanyue) BEIJING, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- China's economy picked up pace in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, supported by fast-growing new drivers and fresh policy support, staying on track to meet its annual growth target and remaining a leading engine of global growth. China's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.5 percent year on year in Q3, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed Monday. The world's second-largest economy generated about 107.11 trillion yuan (about 15.94 trillion U.S. dollars) in output during the January-September period, expanding 4.6 percent year on year, according to the NBS. "The national economy forged ahead against pressure and continued to shift toward innovation-driven, high-quality development, with growing positive changes in major indicators," the NBS said in a statement. China has consistently contributed around 30 percent of global economic growth, with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva saying in January that this contribution is expected to stay at roughly the same level in the coming years. Tourists visit the Anshun ancient town in Anshun City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Oct. 6, 2026. (Photo by Lu Wei/Xinhua) GROWING RESILIENCE Noting that the GDP growth of 4.6 percent in the first three quarters is in line with the country's annual growth target, NBS deputy head Mao Shengyong told a media conference that the economy added 5.7 trillion yuan in output during the period, the largest increase for the same period in the past five years. In the third quarter, GDP growth picked up 0.2 percentage points from the second quarter, while some international institutions expected major economies to grow more slowly in July-September compared to the April-June period, Mao said. There was also a notable rise in momentum on a monthly basis. In September, value-added industrial output rose 5.5 percent year on year, 0.3 percentage points faster than in August, while the services production index gained 4.8 percent, up 0.7 percentage points from the previous month. Retail sales of consumer goods grew 1.1 percent in September, 0.7 percentage points faster than in August, and the surveyed urban unemployment rate edged down 0.1 percentage points from August to 5.2 percent. "Growth momentum showed signs of marginal improvement in September," said Wen Bin, chief economist with China Minsheng Bank, citing faster industrial and services output, a rebound in consumption and an initial stabilization of investment. China will step up efforts to expand domestic demand, improve supply, and make macro policies more effective to sustain the positive momentum of innovation-led and high-quality development, Mao said. To this end, China has recently rolled out a batch of new policies, including financial and fiscal support. "With existing policies being implemented faster and incremental policies gradually taking effect, the economy is expected to continue improving in the fourth quarter," Wen said. Humanoid robots are seen under training at an intelligent manufacturing plant for commercial vehicles of the Dongfeng Liuzhou Motor in Liuzhou City, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Jan. 30, 2026. (Photo by Zheng Changhao/Xinhua) NEW DRIVERS AT WORK New growth drivers continued to expand, contributing more than 40 percent to China's economic growth in the first three quarters. Value-added industrial output rose 5.3 percent year on year, with equipment manufacturing up 10.2 percent and high-tech manufacturing up 14.3 percent. Output of industrial robots, lithium-ion batteries and 3D printing equipment jumped 29.1 percent, 39.5 percent and 62.5 percent, respectively. Monday's data also showed that the services sector expanded 5.2 percent year on year in the first three quarters, with information transmission, software and IT services up 10.4 percent, and leasing and business services up 12.3 percent. The shift is visible in the economic structure. Manufacturing accounted for 25.7 percent of GDP in the first three quarters, up 0.6 percentage points from a year earlier, while the share of high-tech manufacturing in the value-added output of major industrial enterprises rose 1.6 percentage points. Investment in intellectual property products climbed 9.3 percent. Traditional industries are also moving up the value chain. In Jingdezhen, a ceramics hub in east China's Jiangxi Province, local producers have embraced 3D printing in pottery making, propelling the sector's output to over 100 billion yuan. Meanwhile, some coal mining companies have implemented smart monitoring systems for underground operations, increasing efficiency by 30 percent. Green development is creating openings as well. The penetration rate of new energy vehicles in China has stayed above 60 percent for six consecutive months, while the country's energy consumption per unit of GDP fell 3.1 percent in the first three quarters. "The foundations of the economy remain solid, while new quality productive forces, modern services and high-tech foreign trade are steadily taking root," said Zhu Qigui, associate director of the China Academy of Financial Research. "As long as China continues to rely on innovation, reform and its vast market, the trend of moving toward new and better development will not change," the scholar said. A drone photo shows new energy vehicles to be exported at Yantai Port in east China's Shandong Province, Sept. 15, 2026. (Photo by Tang Ke/Xinhua) SHARED OPPORTUNITIES A major trading partner of as many as 169 countries and regions, China saw its goods trade rise 18.8 percent year on year to 39.94 trillion yuan in the first three quarters. In September alone, trade grew 27.5 percent. In the first nine months, exports of mechanical and electrical products climbed 23.7 percent and accounted for 64.3 percent of total exports, while intermediate goods made up more than half of all exports, reinforcing China's role as a stabilizing anchor for global industrial and supply chains. In east China's Anhui Province, robotics manufacturer EFORT Intelligent Robot Co., Ltd. has continued to see growth in overseas orders this year, with a batch of its spraying robots set to be exported to Italy. The company's overseas revenue increased by more than 50 percent year on year in the first half of 2026. Meanwhile, the company's client, German automobile giant Volkswagen, is shifting its strategy from "in China, for China" to "in China, beyond China," with cars produced in China already exported to the Middle East and Central Asia. Foreign-invested enterprises in China remained active players in the January-September period, with their imports and exports rising 19 percent to 11.69 trillion yuan, a record high for the same period. Their trade in intermediate goods grew 27.4 percent to 7.9 trillion yuan, and their high-tech product exports jumped 42.1 percent. More foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0," deepening their integration into China's industrial and innovation chains, Mao said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China's Central Archives opens over 5,000 Long March items to mark 90th anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
China's Central Archives opens over 5,000 Long March items to mark 90th anniversary China's Central Archives opens more than 5,000 Long March-related archival items to the public on October 19, 2026 to mark the 90th anniversary of the Red Army's Long March victory. Photo: CCTV News China's Central Archives opened more than 5,000 Long March-related archival items to the public on Monday to mark the 90th anniversary of the Red Army's Long March victory, offering firsthand accounts of key battles, strategic decisions and solidarity between soldiers and civilians, according to China Central Television (CCTV) News. The newly accessible materials mainly date from October 1934 to October 1936, including include programs and declarations issued by the Communist Party of China, Red Army telegrams and reports on operational deployments, and revolutionary newspapers and periodicals founded and published by the Party. Together, they showcase the revolutionary spirit of the CPC and the people's armed forces, vividly depicting how the Red Army and ordinary people stood united, braved sacrifice and pressed ahead during the Long March, according to CCTV News. Among the materials opened to the public for the first time is Jiebao (victory bulletin), a newspaper founded by the CPC's Shanghai central bureau. A total of 40 issues were published between October 1933 and June 1935, exposing the reactionary rule of the Kuomintang, publicizing the Red Army's military achievements and development in the revolutionary base areas. Liu Kun, a staff member of the Central Archives' archival access department, was cited as saying that "the December 17, 1934, issue of Jiebao carried a report stating, 'The westward-bound Red Army has victoriously captured Liping in Guizhou' … Liping was the site of the first Political Bureau meeting held by the CPC Central Committee after the Long March began. The Liping Meeting affirmed the decision to change course at Tongdao and established the Red Army's strategy of advancing westward, thereby averting the risk of being encircled and annihilated by Kuomintang forces had it continued north." The words "utmost urgency" on the telegram testify to the critical military situation at the time. Another document, titled "Report on the first division's covering of the entire army's bridge crossing tomorrow," provides a detailed account of the Red Army's exploits in capturing Luding Bridge, said Liu. "The capture of Luding Bridge was one of the major victories of strategic significance during the Red Army's Long March," Liu said. "As a firsthand battlefield record, this document details when units of the first red army corps arrived at Luding Bridge and launched their attacks. It also records the situation on the ground as they captured the bridge, defeated a regiment of Sichuan troops and seized military supplies. The document states, 'Today, we captured more than 100 prisoners and over 100 firearms, along with enough ammunition and hand grenades to substantially replenish our supplies.'" The 25th Red Army set out from Hejiachong in Luoshan county, Henan Province, on November 16, 1934, and arrived in Yongping, Shaanxi Province, on September 15, 1935, to become the first Red Army force to reach northern Shaanxi during the Long March. A special report submitted to the CPC Central Committee on July 17, 1935, by Wu Huanxian, the political commissar of the 25th Red Army, is an important historical source for research into the force's Long March. "In this report, Wu perceptively raised the question of whether they could join forces with the 26th and 28th armies, concentrate their strength to destroy enemy forces, support the main Red Army's operations in the northwest, and swiftly establish a new, strong and consolidated revolutionary base there," Liu said. "Operating in isolation, without instructions from the CPC Central Committee or deployments ordered by higher authorities, the CPC Hubei-Henan-Shaanxi Provincial Committee resolutely decided that the main force of the 25th Red Army should advance westward and northward to support the main Red Army. Wu's report also explains the thinking behind that decision," Liu said. Starting Monday, audiences can consult these materials at the Central Archives' public reading hall by presenting valid identification, such as a national ID card or work ID, per CCTV News. item.title: China leads the world in innovation clusters
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
China leads the world in innovation clusters A talent cooperation and exchange conference for the Yangtze River Delta G60 Science and Technology Innovation Corridor is held in Jinhua, east China's Zhejiang province, April 28, 2026. (Photo/Huang Wenlong) The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) recently released its 2026 ranking of the world's top 100 innovation clusters. China accounted for 25 clusters on the list, ranking first globally for the fourth consecutive year. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou, Beijing, and Shanghai-Suzhou clusters all ranked among the top 10. The ranking identifies regions with concentrated innovation activity based on indicators including international patent applications, scientific publications, and venture capital transactions. China's consistent strong showing on the list, with innovation clusters flourishing across multiple regions, demonstrates both the scale and depth of its innovation ecosystem. This leadership reflects years of strategic investment in coordinated regional tech development. Regional innovation networks have become a key pillar of the national innovation framework and provide a vital foundation for building China into a leading country in science and technology. Coordinated development in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region has fostered deeper collaboration, with Beijing focusing on research and development while Tianjin and Hebei translate research findings into manufacturing applications. Meanwhile, the integrated development of the Yangtze River Delta has strengthened links among innovation hubs along the G60 Science and Technology Innovation Corridor, creating a cross-regional collaborative innovation platform spanning nine cities. Stronger regional collaboration has cultivated a sound pattern of innovation with multiple hubs working in concert. Beyond sheer numbers, the rankings also signal a comprehensive upgrade across China's broader innovation system. Innovation clusters capture the close links among research institutions, businesses, talent, and investment. In recent years, China has accelerated the commercialization of scientific and technological advances while nurturing and expanding new quality productive forces. Many of the innovation clusters on the list are also major industrial hubs. Wuhan in central China's Hubei province, ranked 17th, saw the value added of its industrial enterprises above the designated size in high-tech manufacturing rise 65.7 percent year on year in the first half of this year, as its optoelectronics and information technology industries gathered pace. Ningde in Fujian province, meanwhile, climbed 24 places in the rankings, driven in large part by innovation in its power battery industry. Photo shows the DeepBlue Technology Park in Dapeng New District, Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province. (Photo/Li Jianqiang) This virtuous cycle between innovation and development is enabling more emerging and future-oriented industries to gain momentum and grow rapidly within these clusters. China's leading position in the number of top 100 global innovation clusters is also creating valuable opportunities for global partners. An increasing number of foreign-invested companies are choosing to conduct research and pursue innovation in China, with many establishing R&D centers in these clusters. In the first seven months of this year, foreign applicants filed more than 42,000 invention patent applications in China. In 2025, foreign investment actually utilized in scientific research and technical services accounted for nearly 1/5 of China's total utilized foreign investment. China is also committed to sharing the benefits of innovation through openness and cooperation. In the first half of this year, Chinese developers of innovative drugs reached 81 licensing deals with overseas partners, while industrial robots made in China were exported to 141 countries and regions. As Carsten Fink, WIPO's chief economist, noted, Chinese innovation is pushing the frontiers of global science and technology across an expanding range of fields, with countries around the world increasingly benefiting from it. Photo shows Taicang Biomedical Industrial Park in east China's Jiangsu province. (Photo/Ji Haixin) Today, global innovation resources are increasingly converging on China through its innovation clusters. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Chinese premier says ready to expand cooperation with Tajikistan in emerging industries
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Chinese premier says ready to expand cooperation with Tajikistan in emerging industries DUSHANBE, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said Monday that China is willing to expand cooperation with Tajikistan in emerging industries such as the digital economy and artificial intelligence. In his meeting with Tajik President Emomali Rahmon, Li said China stands ready to expand bilateral trade with Tajikistan, strengthen cooperation in infrastructure, green minerals, connectivity and other fields, so as to jointly build new drivers of economic growth. He called for deepening cooperation with Tajikistan in law enforcement and security, saying both sides should strengthen intelligence exchanges and information sharing, jointly combat the three forces of terrorism, separatism and extremism, and safeguard lasting peace and stability in the region. The Chinese premier expressed hope that the Tajik side will continue to take strong measures to ensure the safety and security of Chinese personnel and enterprises in Tajikistan. Li arrived here on Sunday for an official visit to Tajikistan and the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO). In talks with the Tajik president, he said China will fully support Tajikistan in successfully hosting the SCO meeting, and stands ready to work with all parties to promote higher-quality development of the SCO. China is also willing to strengthen communication and coordination with Tajikistan within the United Nations, the China-Central Asia mechanism and other multilateral frameworks, actively implement the four global initiatives proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity, he said. The premier noted that China and Tajikistan are currently advancing efforts to build a community with a shared future between the two countries, and in May this year, President Xi met with President Rahmon, providing further guidance for the development of bilateral relations. China cherishes its profound friendship with Tajikistan and will always view China-Tajikistan relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, Li said. China stands ready to consolidate and deepen political mutual trust with Tajikistan, firmly support each other's core interests, continuously enhance the quality and effectiveness of cooperation, and continue to work hand in hand on the path toward modernization, he added. item.title: 5,300-square-meter flower display draws crowds in Xiamen
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
5,300-square-meter flower display draws crowds in Xiamen Photo shows an aerial view of a 5,300-square-meter flower display at Xiamen Horticulture Expo Garden in Jimei district, Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian Province. (People's Daily Online/Chen Bo) A vibrant sea of autumn flowers spanning 5,300 square meters is in full bloom on Haiyang Island at Xiamen Horticulture Expo Garden in Jimei district, Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian Province, attracting large numbers of visitors. More than 10 kinds of flowers bloom across the island, among them cockscombs, globe amaranths, Egyptian starclusters, begonias and Siam tulips. Red, yellow, orange, blue and pink stand out against green trees, clear water and open sky, with the city beyond. Visitors weave along the paths through the flower beds. Some stop to photograph the blooms, while others stroll on with family and friends. A visitor surnamed Wang, from Shenyang in northeast China's Liaoning Province, said she had made a point of visiting the flower display during her National Day trip to Xiamen after seeing it on social media. She said the blooms made her autumn sightseeing trip especially enjoyable, and that even her casual snapshots came out looking impressive. item.title: China's former revolutionary base areas embrace new chapter of development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
China's former revolutionary base areas embrace new chapter of development Photo shows the Jiajin Mountain Tunnel in southwest China's Sichuan province. (Photo from People's Daily app) Two bridges over the Huajiang River in southwest China's Guizhou province offer a striking glimpse into the remarkable transformation of China's former revolutionary base areas. The first is the Huajiang Chain Bridge. With its iron chains and wooden-plank deck, it spans a section of the Beipan River. In 1935, as the Right-Flank Column of the Central Red Army advanced into southwestern Guizhou, the 11th Regiment of the Third Red Army Corps held its position here, buying precious time for the main force. This wartime lifeline embodied the determination to overcome every challenge and fight for victory. The other one, the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge, is pushing the boundaries of bridge construction in mountainous terrain through intelligent construction, innovative materials, advanced wind-resistant designs, and environmentally friendly building techniques. Its construction, which has set multiple world records, has effectively bridged the "gaps" created by the mountains and canyons. The old and new bridges now stand within sight of each other, offering a vivid picture of how former revolutionary base areas have changed, and Guizhou is far from the only example. The opening of flights at Ruijin Airport in east China's Jiangxi province has given people in southern Jiangxi and western Fujian, both former revolutionary base areas, a new "air corridor" linking them with the rest of the country. The Jiajin Mountain Tunnel in southwest China's Sichuan province has entered trial operation, turning the arduous journey "over" the mountain into a smooth passage "through" it and freeing local residents from worries about mountain closures caused by winter snow and ice. Bridges spanning valleys, passenger planes roaring overhead, and tunnels piercing through mountains -- the path to modernization for old revolutionary base areas is growing ever broader. Photo shows the Huajiang Grand Valley Bridge in southwest China's Guizhou province. (Photo/Li Yunfeng) What is driving these once-remote areas to take on a new look? Major undertakings call for riding the tide of the times. Development anchored in the prevailing trends of the era ensures the right direction and provides a strong driving force. That once-remote regions are no longer isolated, and less-developed areas no longer lag behind, owes much to their ability to seize opportunities of the times and align themselves with broader development trends. Deep in the mountains of Baisha township in Jishui county, Jiangxi province, fruit farmers are now able to sell their produce through livestreaming. This mountain hamlet, where people once "shouted to communicate and traveled on foot", is now equipped with 5G base stations, bringing new vitality to rural revitalization. Today, China boasts nearly 4.6 million 5G base stations and over 30.53 million gigabit-capable network ports, achieving gigabit-level connectivity for every county and 5G coverage in every township. From snow-capped mountains peaks to seashores, from the depth of dense forests to desert steppes, digital infrastructure functions like an intricate neural network, bridging the digital divide and bringing the benefits of digital and intelligent technologies to every corner of the country. For many regions, abundant resources and convenient locations offer a head start. Yet experience shows that the availability or scarcity of resources and other factors of production is never an absolute determinant. With the right approach and by building on their own strengths, regions can turn limitations into new advantages and cultivate new growth drivers from what they already have. During the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression, the people and soldiers of the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region stepped up production to break the enemy's blockade, turning Qingyang in Gansu into the "granary of eastern Gansu." Today, Qingyang has once again taken stock of its strengths, drawing on its abundant energy resources and cool climate to develop data centers. Massive volumes of data can travel from Shanghai to the city in a matter of seconds, while computing power in Qingyang enables entrepreneurs in Guangdong in south China to render 3D models at high speed. As server lights replace oil lamps and streams of digital data flow across the land, data and computing power have become a new kind of "grain," helping drive local development while serving the needs of the country as a whole. Industrial upgrading and regional development both require a focus on local strengths and core industries, as well as openness to wider cooperation and integration. Photo shows the Huajiang Chain Bridge. (Photo from the official account of the media center of Zhenfeng county, Guizhou province on WeChat) The Fujian-Ningxia collaboration is a case in point. New forms of cooperation, such as "Fujian enterprises + Ningxia resources" and "Fujian headquarters + Ningxia production bases," are deepening and expanding. Freight trains under Ningxia's multimodal transport "single-document system," a system featuring one unified transport document covering the entire journey across different transport modes, carry full loads of goods bound for Fujian, Guangdong and beyond. Mountains and seas no longer stand as barriers. What began as one-way assistance has evolved into two-way mutual collaboration. Cross-regional reconfiguration of production factors has made regional cooperation more resilient and substantive. From the transformation of former revolutionary base areas to coordinated progress across regions, and from these changes to the steady and high-quality growth of China's economy, China is continuing along its Long March in the new era, moving forward with courage and opening up new horizons. item.title: Shenzhen ready to welcome APEC
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Shenzhen ready to welcome APEC The atmosphere for the major APEC event builds in Shenzhen. (People's Daily Online/Wang Xing) The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18 and 19. It will be the third time China hosts the event. Shenzhen is stepping up preparations in areas ranging from border crossing and public services to public participation, aiming to make travel and daily life more convenient for delegates and international visitors. The Huanggang Port Joint Inspection Building begins operation. (People's Daily Online/Wang Xing) Upgraded ports of entry improve travel efficiency On Oct. 12, the redeveloped Huanggang Port, China's largest single port building and the world's largest land port complex, officially opened for operations. The port implements the colocation arrangement and the novel "collaborative inspection and joint clearance" mode, offering round-the-clock clearance services for cross-border passengers and vehicles. On its first day of operation, the facility handled 79,500 passenger crossings. Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport is piloting an advance screening procedure that has cut passenger entry clearance time during peak periods from 45 minutes to under 15 minutes. Nearly 400 new signs in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and other languages have also been installed. As of early September, the number of foreign passenger trips through the airport from APEC member economies this year had exceeded one million, a record for the same period. The airport operates more than 30 passenger routes to key APEC cities, with over 700 inbound and outbound flights scheduled each week. Photo shows a Chinese-English public sign in Shenzhen. (People's Daily Online/Wang Xing) Better services make Shenzhen more accessible to international visitors Shenzhen is continuing to improve services for international visitors, including foreign-language signage, transportation, payment and tax refunds. Effective Oct. 1, regulations on the standardized use and management of foreign-language public signs set out requirements for signage in eight categories of public places, helping create a more accessible language environment. More than 7,000 smart translation devices have been deployed at bus and subway stations, government service halls, cultural venues and sports facilities across Shenzhen. Over 5,000 taxis are equipped with AI-powered devices that support real-time voice translation in more than 140 languages. English names are available at all 11,000 bus stops across the city, and passengers can scan QR codes on bus-stop signs to access route information in English and real-time arrival updates. For payments, all 17 metro lines and 432 stations in the city accept contactless payments with overseas bank cards. As of July, 41,000 merchants across the city accepted overseas bank cards, supported by 51,000 point-of-sale terminals. From January to August, foreign nationals made 143 million transactions in Shenzhen, totaling 21.09 billion yuan ($3.15 billion), up 18.64 percent and 26.58 percent year on year, respectively. Shenzhen is also expanding services such as departure tax refunds and currency exchange at its airport and in commercial districts. Hospitals, hotels, tourist attractions and legal service providers are working to improve their services for international visitors and clients. Shenzhen residents sign their names on a signature board to show support for green mobility. (People's Daily Online/Wang Xing) Residents join preparations to welcome the Asia-Pacific gathering On Oct. 15, Shenzhen launched a green mobility initiative encouraging residents to reduce or suspend private car use during APEC meeting week. Within three hours of the initiative's launch, more than 20,000 car owners had registered to keep their vehicles off the road. By the morning of Oct. 17, the number had exceeded 230,000. Fourteen universities in Shenzhen, including Shenzhen University and the Southern University of Science and Technology, have established volunteer teams for APEC-related services. International volunteers are active in markets and communities, while student volunteers from Shenzhen Foreign Languages School have been helping foreign visitors navigate Shenzhen North Railway Station and answering their questions. Civil servants are also taking part in safety inspections at the community level, promoting orderly traffic, guiding visitors at venues and supporting international exchange activities. Freight drivers have formed a city volunteer service team, while couriers and food delivery riders are attending classes to learn basic foreign languages and protocol for interacting with international visitors. From border clearance and everyday public services to green mobility and volunteer assistance, Shenzhen is continuing to improve its international services as it prepares to host the APEC meeting.
